claims.claim: Reviewers report technical issues involving game crashes, with some experiencing crashes that also cause the Steam application to close.

citations.review_text: i  cannot play this game on linux it just crashes as soon as it opens and i have the requirements. idk whats happening and i cant fix it please fix this i spent 10 dollars on this

I was recommended to try this game by a friend, and had high expectations for this. Full disclosure I do *not* like puzzles, however I went in with an open mind and was willing to try it, in all honesty it’s a fun game, it’s, to my understanding, very short levels, usually taking a few minutes, I found only the mid-late(?) half to require critical thinking


In honesty I wasn’t actually able to finish the game, I kept experiencing crashes, which is one thing, but I could look past it if it wasn’t so frequent, I had 5 crashes in an hour, however, not only did the game itself crash, my entire Steam application did as well, this is isolated to Portal and I have never seen, nor heard of this anywhere other than Portal.

I ran tests, found fixes, and attempted them, none of which worked. Eventually, after the 5th crash total, I knew that this was a lost cause, considering I’d only get 10-20 minutes of playtime before Steam crashed, I ended up submitting a refund. It was a fun little game, my “not reccomended” isn’t entirely so, I’m moreso 60/40, however no such option exists on Steam. 

If you pick up this game, be aware that this game has the chance to crash frequently, it may not happen to you, or it may, just keep it in mind that if it crashes, your entire Steam app will too, if you don’t get crashes, by all means enjoy a very simplistic puzzle game that will get your cogs turning!

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that the game features clean white walls and tile surfaces that provide plenty of areas to fire the portal gun.

citations.review_text:
[i]portal feels like a dream designed by a machine that doesn’t understand dreams.[/i]

portal is described as a puzzle game first. a clever game. a physics game. a game about momentum and impossible architecture. but none of those descriptions ever fully capture the strange emotional silence sitting underneath it. the mechanics are only the surface layer—clean white walls, portals opening like wounds in reality, test chambers arranged with obsessive precision. underneath that is something colder. something lonely.

it's not just about using a weapon to create 'doors' on walls while listening to a robot’s voice. portal is an experience of solitude where you wake up in an unknown place, voiceless, listening to a synthetic artificial construct trying to imitate human behavior. everything in the game feels manufactured to resemble comfort without actually understanding it. the clean rooms. the calm instructions. the jokes. the fake politeness. it all feels like a machine attempting to reconstruct humanity from observation alone. and that’s what makes the atmosphere so unsettling.

most games want you to feel important. portal barely acknowledges you as a person. you are simply moved from room to room like an object inside a laboratory. nobody asks who you are. nobody explains why you’re there. there are no emotional introductions, no dramatic speeches, no attempts to build attachment. the game trusts emptiness more than exposition. story makes sense in its emptiness—and it does not.

the narrative is fragmented in a way that feels accidental, yet perfectly intentional. you collect pieces of meaning through abandoned corners, hidden graffiti, strange glitches in the environment, moments where the sterile perfection of the facility begins to rot at the edges. you start realizing that the world outside your immediate path exists, but only barely. like memories erased halfway through deletion.

the abandoned maintenance rooms are probably more disturbing than anything expl…

[H3] A more condensed, focused vision than Portal 2. [/H3]

Despite Portal 2 being a critically acclaimed masterpiece, I always felt the dilapidated Aperture research centre was a missed opportunity. The broken walls, doors and larger areas - which should encourage exploration - instead mostly led to invisible walls or broken tiles which you couldn’t interact with or fire your portal gun against. I also felt the formula begin to tire, and the new gameplay mechanics introduced didn’t reinvent the wheel enough to justify an additional 9-10 hours.

The original Portal, on the other hand, feels like a much tighter and curated experience. The short length of 3 hours means each chamber brings about a fresh new challenge, without rehashing or recycling concepts from previous rooms. In Portal 2, I felt several puzzles relying on controller skill and minor adjustments in movement as opposed to solving the underlying problem presented. Portal 1, meanwhile, gets to the heart of the puzzle’s challenges and is less fussed about how well you can use the controller.

Owing to the pristineness of the Aperture lab in the original game, you have more clean tiles to fire your portal gun against too. This makes the levels feel less linear, and despite being caged in, the game actually feels more of a sandbox as a result. Story takes a backseat too, but I always found the minimal narrative creates more intrigue and mystery. Portal 2 shows and explains the plot in strict detail, removing the mystery, while Portal 1 keeps things ambiguous and more thought-provoking.

Portal 1 is a tighter experience which gets immediately to the heart of what makes the series great. It’s also completely free to boot - woo!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game has a short duration.

citations.review_text: Paid a buck fifty and beat it in 90 minutes, which makes it right about on par with my minimum hours of entertainment per dollar spent. Excellent games go beyond that. In this case, there are bonus challenges you can pursue, but the main game itself is extremely short. In the reviews, you can see plenty of people got a lot more than 90 minutes out of it. Maybe you're one of them, but my recommendation is to get it on a great sale.

The game is... fine at best. There are lots of references to Half-Life/Black Mesa, but I haven't played those games yet, so I wasn't able to make much of the connections. The story is fine; it's not overly complicated for someone who goes in blind playing this game. My only problem with this game is that there are just some rooms where the puzzle solutions are... questionable. There are loads of times playing this game made me wonder, "Is that how I'm supposed to do it?" 

The final room where you fight GLaDOS is a flawless sequence in this flawed game (minus the timer; it is a bit too long for me to actually feel threatened by it, but nevertheless, it is flawless). My only critique is how short it is, but perhaps Portal 2 will fix that.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game is relatively short and can be completed within a few hours.

citations.review_text: Portal 2 is obviously the big boy here between the two Portal games, but I still would recommend checking out this game, as it acts as a pretty decent setup to the second game, and certainly gets your brain warmed up for the portal mechanics in both games. Plus with it only taking like 2-3 hours to beat(less for me on here cause I beat it on another account before), its $10 price point is not all that bad(also given that the gameplay itself is actually fun). While obviously not perfect and a bit buggy here and there, it still was a fun little experience to play through.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as relatively short, noting it can be completed in a few hours.

citations.review_text: Very worth the money, I think its only a few bucks for this masterpiece and it's seemingly always on sale so you should make sure to pick it up. The gameplay is amazing and ahead of its time. If you're looking for a short game that takes around an 1-2 hours to fill up your day portal is perfect. In my opinion the 2nd game is much better but this game is still amazing. Also the end credit song is great. I'm writing this review after like my 4th time playing it, and I'm happy every time.

If you've never played Portal before: please do so now. It's short, but sweet, and each little puzzle is exactly the perfect balance of engaging and leisurely. You'll probably beat this game within three to five hours, and you'll probably enjoy every minute of it.

The dialogue is funny; the robots are cute; the environments are very atmospheric; the gameplay is fun and innovative… Portal is iconic for a reason! ^^

I picked up Portal way back in 2010 as part of the Orange Box goodness (or whatever bundle it was in at the time), and even though my stats show I only knocked out the core story achievements (Lab Rat, Fratricide, Partygoer, and Heartbreaker), it left a massive impression.
This game is pure genius in the smallest package possible. The moment you get the portal gun, everything clicks. The puzzles start simple and ramp up beautifully, teaching you mechanics without ever feeling like a tutorial. By the end, you’re solving rooms that would have seemed impossible an hour earlier. GLaDOS is one of the best video game characters ever—witty, sinister, and hilariously passive-aggressive. The cake is a lie, but the fun is very real.
My playthrough was straightforward: I beat the main campaign and called it there. No advanced maps, no challenge medals, no turret-killing shenanigans or 30,000-foot falls for me. But honestly? The base game is so strong that it didn’t matter. It’s short, sweet, and replayable. The physics, the humor, the “eureka!” moments—Portal nails every single one.
If you’re on the fence, just buy it. Even in 2026 this game holds up perfectly. Short enough for a weekend, memorable enough to stick with you for years. Now if you’ll excuse me, I need to go stare at a companion cube again.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight GLaDOS and her dark humor as a standout element of the game.

citations.review_text: Portal is an absolute masterpiece of game design that seamlessly fuses physics-bending mechanics with a masterclass in dark narrative storytelling. Armed only with a portal gun that tears holes through space, you are thrown into a series of clinical test chambers where solving spatial puzzles requires you to completely rethink momentum and gravity. The gameplay loop is flawless, but it is the passive-aggressive, darkly comedic commentary from the villainous AI, GLaDOS, that elevates the experience into an unforgettable psychological journey. Though it is a short, tightly focused adventure, its brilliant pacing, iconic humor, and perfect execution make it one of the most influential and flawless puzzle games ever created.

Portal gun go pew.

Even after 18 years, Portal still feels surprisingly fresh. The gameplay is simple to understand but incredibly satisfying, and using the portal gun to solve increasingly clever test chambers never gets old. Some of the puzzles can be frustrating at times, but figuring them out always feels rewarding.

I expected the achievements to be much harder to complete, but they ended up being really enjoyable with just the right amount of challenge. The bonus challenge levels are also a lot of fun and add some nice replay value.

What really makes the game stand out is GLaDOS. Her dark humour and constant commentary make an already great puzzle game even more memorable. Short, sweet, perfectly paced, and without a second of wasted time.

[spoiler]R.I.P. Companion Cube (Test Chamber 17 – Test Chamber 17) — you will be missed.[/spoiler]

[i]The cake is a lie.[/i] 9.2/10

[h1] THE BIRTH OF A PUZZLE MASTERPIECE [/h1]

[b][i]  A short, brilliant, and absolutely flawless puzzle game that completely redefined first-person mechanics. Armed with nothing but a portal gun, navigating the sterile test chambers of Aperture Science feels incredibly rewarding as the physics-based puzzles constantly challenge your spatial awareness.

The game’s true genius lies in its dark, cynical humor and the introduction of GLaDOS, one of the most iconic and brilliantly written antagonists in video game history. A tight, perfectly paced masterpiece with zero filler.

The cake is a lie. 9.5/10  [/i][/b]

citations.review_text: very fun challenge works well on older laptops

It's super fun and quick, being able to be completed in one sitting. The portal mechanic is absolutely mind boggling when you look at when the game released (seriously, how do you even code that?). It also runs incredibly well, meaning you can play it on practically any device despite its (in my opinion) good graphics.

Very good! and what id call old but gold now. definitely worth playing. i played the second one first on the ps3 but the first one is probably my favorite for setting the basics for portal and what the second game followed on, really good story amazing value if you can get it when its on sale for pretty cheap. if you have lower powered hardware it should work fine as with most older valve games.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention experiencing motion sickness while playing the game.

citations.review_text: it’s a really cool puzzle game, but i wouldn’t recommend it if you’re prone to motion sickness. this was the first game that actually made me feel nauseous (never had that happen before). after looking around, i found quite a few people who had the same experience. turns out i wasn’t the only one suffering. some also mentioned that playing on the Steam Deck can make it worse bc the smaller field of view in FPS games turns your eyeballs into washing machines. i haven’t tried it on PC yet, but a number of players recommend increasing the FOV, which apparently helps. thankfully, i got used to it after a while and the motion sickness became much more manageable… until Test Chamber 18. i went in fine and came out spiritually rotated :)

In 2007, Valve created a first-person puzzler where you alter the world using portals in a fantastically neat package. It's bursting at the seams with lore and story development; and became an online cultural icon. Valve is an annoying game developer because so many of its titles become genre defining works, yet they also push the limits of what mechanics can be present in video game software. It's unfair that, while being nearly 20 years old, this game still plays incredibly.

You'll become a little motion sick, but at least you'll learn why the cake is a lie!
Incredible game but if you get motion sick easily watch out

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the bonus challenge maps and advanced levels provide a significant and sometimes frustrating spike in difficulty compared to the main campaign.

citations.review_text: I LOVE PORTAL. I'm going to be so honest though; It is infuriating at times, especially the advanced bonus levels because they depend on physical skill and patience over mental problem solving. Still, it is one of my favorite games of all time you should play it. Always remember: the cake is a lie.

I've finally 100%:ed the game, and now I will give my conclusion on this game.

Well, it plays around a superb mechanic (that being the portals. I love portals in this game), good humor and story, and is certainly a very fun and short game for you to enjoy during a weekend, or to prepare for the sequel. It is made by Valve during their game development era, so expect good stuff and a sometimes buggy "Source" engine.

But if you are interested in 100%:ing this game, then let me tell you: Most achievements are okay and fun to do, even though some of them acts as a treasure hunt where you need to do some very specific stuff. but this is only after you beat the game once but still fun nonetheless. So pretty much this, doing achievements during the campaign is a blast, some of them will be acquired by just progressing, while others requiring you to do some certain interactions.
But then there is the bonus maps that contain 2 different groups of levels: Advanced maps and "Challenge maps". The former is a fun one, because it remixes some levels from the campaign and makes the harder. But the latter group however, is the most notorious, obnoxious, stupidly difficult and physics-dependent challenge in any game that I've ever played. Or atleast one of the challenges are.
Well you see, each of all 6 maps in Challenge maps (which are the same as 6 maps from the campaign) have 3 different challenges. These are "least portal", "least steps" and "least time". The first one is actually fun and behaves like a very hardcore puzzle if you wanna get the "gold medals". The third one is a bit annoying because it requires good movement in the Source engine and some speedrun strats but still very achievable. But oh no, the second one, the "least steps" is STUPID AS FROGG!! It requires you to beat the level with as few; no, not the DISTANCE of your movement, but instead EVERY INSTANCE YOU MOVE BY ANY TYPE OF PHYSICS. This means that if you just click a direction for a split millisecon…

★★★★★

Valves 2007 puzzle masterpiece was such a sick experience, as someone who hasn't really played portal 2, nor portal 1 at all i came into this completely blind without much forward thinking. At first i was genuinely stumped at how half of this game worked but as i went along the more i understood the in's and outs of the physics and thinking required to actually succeed in the Aperture Science Laboratories. I can absolutely understand why this is the fifth highest rated steam game oat as its just such a fun unique AND innovative contribution to the puzzle genres. Coming from this experience im very very excited for portal 2 as that game seems like it builds upon the first game and makes it 100x better.

The 100% while short was pretty difficult for me as the advanced levels kicked my ass. Base game levels took like an hour and the other 5-6 hours was spent on doing my second playthrough along with the advanced levels. The challenge levels were my biggest issue as im useless at everything speedrunning related so i had to cop out with that and cheese it. HOWEVER the rest is honestly to a normal player pretty achievable and you can have quite a lot of fun whilst doing it. Achievements like Terminal Velocity and Friendly fire are just goofy and fun and something that you would do out of pure curiousity and experimenting. HOWEVER the radio achievement was less than delightful to do and i was not that much of a fan of it. 

All in all i feel like whatever i say has already been said about portal, i came into this game kinda not liking it and the more i played the more i loved and cherished the really enjoyed the physics and quirks of the old valve games. Its charming and fun and affordable normally and on sale its an absolute bargain. Hope to have more fun with this as time goes on

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game is short in length.

citations.review_text: This game is perfect if you want a short puzzle game with evil robots. And Weighted Companion Cube.

As someone who replays this game [b]every year[/b], I can confidently say that Portal never gets old.

Despite its short length, every test chamber is brilliantly designed, the mechanics are introduced at the perfect pace, and the game never overstays its welcome. Solving puzzles with the portal gun is just as satisfying today as it was when I had my first playthrough.

The writing is excellent, GLaDOS is one of the most memorable villains in gaming, and the humor still lands after countless playthroughs. Even knowing every solution by heart doesn't take away from the experience.

If you somehow haven't played Portal yet, do yourself a favor and fix that. It's one of the best puzzle games ever made.

[b]The cake may be a lie, but this masterpiece isn't.[/b]
